sentences.text: This massive dinosaur measured approximately 10 meters in length and stood 3 meters tall.
Unlike many relatives, the large thumb claw of Lamplughsaura was not particularly curved.
Kutty and his colleagues formally described Lamplughsaura dharmaramensis as a new genus and species in 2007.
The genus name Lamplughsaura honors Pamela Lamplugh Robinson, who founded the Geological Studies Unit at the Indian Statistical Institute in Kolkata.
The disarticulated position of cranial elements suggests that some Lamplughsaura specimens were skeletally immature.
Fused neurocentral sutures on caudal vertebrae suggest that the specimens represent subadult individuals.
Lamplughsaura likely coexisted with the sauropodomorph Pradhania gracilis in the Upper Dharmaram Formation.
Lamplughsaura was likely preyed upon by an indeterminate theropod resembling Dilophosaurus.
Lamplughsaura is considered a basal sauropod or sauropodomorph, more closely related to Blikanasaurus and Melanorosaurus.
Lamplughsaura belongs to the unranked clade Anchisauria.
Lamplughsaura lived during the Sinemurian age of the Early Jurassic in the Dharmaram Formation of India, approximately 190 million years ago.
The time range for Lamplughsaura is estimated from 201.4 to 192.9 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
